struct WeightedEdge { std::ptrdiff_t from; std::ptrdiff_t to; std::int64_t weight; }

This is Dijkstra's algorithm. Track the shortest distance found so far to every station, and repeatedly settle the closest station not yet settled: once a station is popped with the smallest distance remaining in the frontier, no corridor still unexplored can offer it anything shorter, because every corridor length is positive. A min heap of
pairs is what lets "closest not yet settled" come out in O(log n) instead of a scan over every station on each step.

Every station enters the heap at most once per corridor that improves its distance, so the run is O((n + m) log n) time and O(n + m) space for the adjacency list and the heap. The edge cases are a start station with no corridors, and a station, index 5 above, that no corridor reaches at all, which stays no value. Skipping a popped entry whose distance no longer matches the best on record is what keeps a station from being processed twice after a shorter route to it is found later.
